newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh SEC bars brokers as company directors.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh SEC bars brokers as company directors.

text.p: Bangladesh's Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has barred stock brokers from being directors of companies listed on stock exchanges.
The SEC issued the directive to all the listed companies and authorities of the two bourses in Dhaka and Chittagong.
SEC Chairman Haroon-ur Rashid told Reuters the restrictions were aimed at preventing brokers from manipulating share prices.
"Nowhere in the world brokers could become directors of the listed companies because they know in advance price sensitive information of the companies and are able to manipulate prices," he said.
"From now on, they have to choose between the two -- either being owner of the company or stock trader."

"Consequent to the amendments to the Securities and Exchange Commission Regulations...no stock broker or dealer can become or can remain as a director of a company listed with a stock exchange of which such broker or dealer is a member," said a directive issued by the SEC, the market watchdog, on November 6 but revealed to the press on Saturday.
The restrictions will come into force immediately and brokers may lose their licences for violation, SEC sources said.
The move comes as the all-share price index at the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) spiralled to well above 3,000. It has doubled in just two months.
The bull run has attracted many investors in the kerb market, despite SEC warnings that trading shares outside the DSE premises could involve many risks.
The DSE officials reacted calmly to the new restrictions.
"It's like curbing our fundamental right. But we will accept it," said DSE Chairman Imtiyaz Hosain.
Some top DSE brokers are directors of many listed companies, SEC officials said without giving details.
Foreign fund managers have often complained that the Bangladesh stock market lacked transparency and proper regulation.
